query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
editable training systems for tool-using agents
text:
1. **EAU: Environment–Agent–User Co-evolution** — The closest match: a meta-agent edits user simulators, environments, rewards, and RL settings during live training. Min Cai and Xi Ye (University of Alberta/Amii); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent).  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523

2. **ScaleEnv** — Automatically constructs editable, executable tool environments and verifiable tasks for agent RL. Dunwei Tu, Yi-Kai Zhang, and Furao Shen (Nanjing University); Hongyan Hao, Hansi Yang, Zhikang Xia, Yu Yang, Yueqing Sun, Qi Gu, Hui Su, and Xunliang Cai (Meituan); Yihao Chen (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen); Xingchen Liu (East China Normal University).  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06820

3. **SMITH: Joint Optimization of Tool Creation and Use** — Trains one policy to create tools, use them, and improve their interfaces from execution feedback. Zhi Rui Tam and Shao-Hua Sun (Appier AI Research and National Taiwan University); Chieh-Yen Lin (Appier AI Research); Yun-Nung Chen and Hung-yi Lee (National Taiwan University).  
   https://tool-use-smith.github.io/

4. **RandomWorld: Procedural Environment Generation for Tool-Use Agents** — Generates interactive tools and compositional tasks programmatically for supervised and reinforcement learning. Michael Sullivan, Mareike Hartmann, and Alexander Koller (Department of Language Science and Technology, Saarland University/Saarland Informatics Campus).  
   https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.936/

5. **Aviary** — An extensible “gymnasium” for defining environments and training tool-using language agents on scientific tasks. Siddharth Narayanan, James D. Braza, Ryan-Rhys Griffiths, Manvitha Ponnapati, Albert Bou, Jon Laurent, Ori Kabeli, Geemi Wellawatte, Sam Cox, Samuel G. Rodriques, and Andrew D. White; affiliations span FutureHouse, the University of Rochester, and the Francis Crick Institute.  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.21154
